groups.title: Error Boundaries
groups.question: One failing widget takes down your whole Remix page, and users see a generic error for a missing project. Explain how error boundaries work in Remix.

followUps.ErrorBoundary in Route Modules: What does a route-level ErrorBoundary catch?
followUps.useRouteError and isRouteErrorResponse: How do you tell a 404 apart from an unexpected crash?

evidence.text: Each route can export an ErrorBoundary.
It catches errors from that route's loader, action and rendering.
Only that part of the page is replaced, while parent layouts keep working.
useRouteError returns what was thrown.
isRouteErrorResponse checks if it was a thrown Response, like a 404.
Expected errors get a friendly message; unexpected ones get a generic message and are logged.

groups.title: Throwing Responses
groups.question: A missing project should show a 'not found' page, and unknown URLs fall through to a generic error. Explain how you would throw expected errors and handle unmatched routes.

followUps.throw new Response() for Expected Errors: Why throw a Response for an expected error like not found?
followUps.404 Handling with Splat Routes: How does a splat route handle unknown URLs?

evidence.text: Throwing a Response with a 4xx status stops the loader.
The ErrorBoundary receives it with its status.
It is treated as an expected error, not logged as a crash.
A splat route matches any URL no other route matched.
It renders a custom 404 page.
It should return a 404 status so search engines know the page does not exist.

notEnough: Only saying it catches all routes.

groups.title: Resilience Patterns
groups.question: A partner API your loader calls sometimes fails briefly and sometimes hangs for 30 seconds. Explain how you would make the loader resilient.

followUps.Retry Logic and Exponential Backoff: When should a loader retry, and how?
followUps.Timeout Patterns with AbortController: How do you stop a slow API from holding up the page?

evidence.text: Brief network failures can succeed on a retry.
Retries wait longer each time, with some randomness.
Retries are limited and only used for safe, repeatable requests.
An AbortController cancels the fetch after a set time.
This frees the server instead of waiting indefinitely.
The page can show a fallback or error when the call times out.

notEnough: Only saying you add a timeout.

groups.title: Logging and Observability
groups.question: Errors happen in production but your logs have no context and nobody is alerted. Explain how you would log and monitor server errors in Remix.

followUps.Structured Error Logging on the Server: What context should a server error log include?
followUps.entry.server.tsx and handleError: What is handleError in entry.server.tsx for?

evidence.text: Errors are logged as structured data, not plain text.
Logs include the user id, route and request id.
That context makes it possible to trace and reproduce the problem.
handleError is the global catch point for unhandled server errors.
It is the place to send errors to a monitoring service like Sentry.
Every unexpected server error is then reported in one place.
